title: Choose the visual world
question: Fresh hand. Everything from the last round is out. The roll assigned Weighbridge Ticket. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Weighbridge Ticket
options.thesis: The homepage is one thermal ticket for the whole operations set: printed on site, still missing from the books.
options.viewport: A landscape ticket filling the browser: D1 lockup in the header stamp, line items for jobs, costing, plant, variations, certificates, and capture; Book a yard visit is the weighbridge stamp at the foot.
options.risk: Reads as civil-only, or as a novelty receipt, and undersells sparkies and fleet.

raised.raise: Nav is numbered boards, not a SaaS mega-menu; the yard visit is the one scarce live connection.
Ops layers stack; peel the field layer and the ledger stays intact underneath.
Capture keeps its dirt: a photographed docket is the proof it came from site, not a typed-clean form.

options.label: Yard Office Whiteboard
options.lineage: morning dispatch boards in South West yards
options.thesis: The homepage is the board they already look at before the first truck leaves.
options.viewport: A landscape enamel board: columns for jobs, plant, variations, certificates, and capture; Book a yard visit is a magnet in the corner; BAD FORM Systems is the printed header strip.
options.risk: This is also where most ops-tool sites land: a kanban that looks like software, not a yard office.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Six needles, one each for jobs, costing, plant, variations, certificates, and capture; the yard is running when they lean together.
options.viewport: A landscape meter bridge as the webpage: six identical VU faces labelled for the ops layer; Book a yard visit sits on the strip below; red is only the arc past zero.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the whole layer is a single sweep. Loses identification: a recording desk is not a South West yard.
options.risk: Reads as another instrument dashboard, one walnut frame from the SaaS miss.

options.label: Numbered Insert Cards
options.lineage: numbered packet insert cards, album sold separately
options.thesis: The ops layer is a numbered set. Xero is the album sold separately. Missing numbers are glovebox dockets.
options.viewport: A landscape album page of six cards: jobs, costing, plant, variations, certificates, capture; one slot empty; Book a yard visit is printed on the reverse of the shown card.
options.case: Holds product clarity: absence is the pitch. Loses identification: trading-card grammar is not this buyer's daily object.
options.risk: Looks like a collector hobby, not a yard visit.

options.label: Botanical Season Folio
options.lineage: botanical plates of one plant through the seasons
options.thesis: Five plates at the same scale: capture, jobs, costing, plant, then Xero; the day is comparable because nothing changes size.
options.viewport: A landscape folio: five registered plates in one row, same job through the day; Book a yard visit is the species-name line.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the field-to-ledger day is a registered sequence. Loses identification: a botanical folio is not this yard.
options.risk: Reads as a nature monograph, and lands in the cream-plate cluster this work is trying to escape.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: Ops layers as numbered boards on an 80-column grid; the yard visit is the one live caller.
options.viewport: A title screen pouring in: BAD FORM Systems as block art, numbered exits for jobs, capture, costing, Xero; Book a yard visit is new mail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a BBS is software theatre, and the owner does not identify with a 2 a.m. phone line.
options.kept: Numbered exits; presence is scarce; the yard visit is the live connection.
options.risk: Looks like a developer toy, which is the miss this buyer named.

options.label: Łowicz Layered Papercut
options.thesis: Ops layers are unmixed colour cuts pasted in order; depth is overlap, never shade; the ledger is the last paste.
options.viewport: A centred roundel of the yard built in six colour layers; Book a yard visit is the last paste.
options.case: Fuses poorly: folk papercut is not this yard's graphic home, and a roundel hides the ops list.
options.kept: Layers paste over each other; removing one exposes the layer below intact.
options.risk: Reads as a craft object, not an operations offer.

options.label: Hand-Processed Film Bloom
options.thesis: Field capture is the emulsion joining the event: scratches and light leaks are proof it came from site.
options.viewport: A film strip of the day's frames: ute, docket, job, Xero draft; Book a yard visit is the edge code.
options.case: Fuses poorly: experimental cinema hides the offer, and this buyer does not identify with a film lab.
options.kept: The photographed event joins the record dirty; capture is not a typed-clean form.
options.risk: Looks like an art-house title sequence.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What SimPRO, Tradify, and AroFlo already look like, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A dark SaaS hero, a job-app screenshot, three feature columns, and Book a yard visit in the header.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
